agents|summarized-memory: Long-running tool workflows can summarize earlier turns to bound context; tool state still needs explicit records because summaries can omit facts.
attention|query-key-value: Queries score keys to decide how strongly their associated values contribute to an attention output.
bag-of-words|language-ai: Bag-of-words is an early text representation for language tasks, useful as a transparent baseline before neural models.
bag-of-words|text-embedding: Bag-of-words counts lexical features; dense text embeddings learn a vector geometry whose similarities depend on training and pooling.
bertopic|class-based-tf-idf: BERTopic can aggregate each cluster into a class document and use c-TF-IDF to identify its distinctive terms.
bertopic|topic-representations: BERTopic separates document clustering from the keywords, labels or examples used to describe each topic.
chain-of-thought|chain-prompting: A reasoning trace can occur inside one completion; chain prompting passes outputs between distinct model calls.
chain-prompting|few-shot-examples: A stage in a prompt chain can include demonstrations, but adding examples does not itself create a multi-call chain.
chain-prompting|self-consistency: A chain can produce several candidate answers for aggregation; voting adds calls and can preserve a shared error.
chain-prompting|tree-of-thought: A prompt chain follows a sequence; tree search branches over candidate reasoning states under an evaluator and budget.
class-based-tf-idf|maximal-marginal-rele: MMR can diversify candidate topic keywords; c-TF-IDF instead weights terms by their specificity to a cluster.
class-based-tf-idf|topic-representations: Distinctive class-level term weights provide one keyword representation of a topic, rather than a new document clustering.
cluster-inspection|topic-modeling: Reading members, outliers and representative documents tests whether a proposed topic label describes its actual cluster.
context-size|decoding: The prompt and generated continuation must share a finite context budget, including reserved output tokens.
context-size|kv-cache: A longer retained context typically requires more cached key/value positions during autoregressive inference.
contextualized-embeddings|text-embedding: A text embedding pools contextual token representations; pooling and the training objective determine the resulting sentence geometry.
contrastive-training|recommendation-embe: Positive and negative item relationships can train recommendation vectors; the definition of a useful neighbor comes from the task data.
cross-attention|sequence-to-sequence: An encoder-decoder model can use decoder queries to attend to keys and values derived from the encoded source.
decoder-only|decoding: A causal decoder supplies next-token scores; the decoding policy chooses how to turn those scores into a continuation.
decoder-only|encoder-only: Causal decoders restrict attention to earlier positions; bidirectional encoders use context on both sides for their intended representation tasks.
decoder-only|generative-model: A decoder-only language model is one architecture for autoregressive generation, not the only possible generative architecture.
decoder-only|kv-cache: During causal generation, cached past keys and values avoid repeatedly recomputing the same prefix projections.
decoder-only|transformer: Decoder-only models use transformer blocks with causal attention rather than an encoder-decoder source/target arrangement.
decoding|generative-model: The trained generator defines token probabilities, while greedy, sampling or search policies select actual output sequences.
decoding|kv-cache: The cache changes inference computation; it should preserve the same decoding outputs within the tested numerical tolerance.
efficient-attention|positional-embedding: Reducing attention memory or changing head layouts still requires a consistent representation of token position.
efficient-attention|transformer-block: Attention optimizations change one component of a transformer block; normalization, residual and feed-forward costs still remain.
embeddings-for-classification|supervised: A supervised classifier can learn a label boundary over fixed sentence vectors instead of updating the whole text encoder.
embeddings-for-classification|task-speci: A task head over cached embeddings and a fine-tuned encoder are different adaptation choices with different latency and label requirements.
encoder-only|text-embedding: An encoder can produce contextual token vectors that a pooling rule converts into a reusable text vector.
encoder-only|transformer: Encoder-only models use transformer blocks with bidirectional attention for their supported representation objectives.
generative-classification|zero-shot-clas: A generator can emit a label without task training; zero-shot classification can also use other mechanisms such as NLI scoring.
generative-evaluation|generative-model: Reference likelihood, decoded task outputs and human judgments measure different aspects of the same generator.
generative-model|model-access: Local and hosted access expose different controls, resource costs and privacy boundaries for a generation model.
generative-model|pretraining: Next-token pretraining fits a broad continuation distribution; it does not by itself demonstrate instruction-following behavior.
generative-model|representation-model: A model used to generate continuations and a model used to produce task features have different output contracts and evaluation criteria.
kv-cache|query-key-value: Autoregressive caches retain past keys and values; the current step still computes the query used to read them.
language-ai|llm: Large language models are one family within language AI, alongside smaller statistical, representation and task-specific methods.
language-ai|tokenization: Many language systems first convert text into token units, but token boundaries are model conventions rather than universal words.
llm|pretraining-and-sft: A pretrained language model can be adapted with instruction demonstrations; the dataset, targets and updated parameters define that adaptation.
llm|transformer: Transformers are the architecture used by the book's language-model examples, while language modeling names the prediction task.
maximal-marginal-relevance|reranking: A reranker scores query relevance; MMR trades relevance against similarity to already selected results to encourage diversity.
model-access|responsible-use: Access choices affect where text is processed, which controls are available and what evidence can be inspected before deployment.
positional-embeddings-and-rope|sequence-: Packing multiple examples requires deliberate position handling as well as boundary-aware attention and loss masks.
pretraining-and-sft|reward-models: An SFT policy can precede preference collection; a separately trained scalar reward model learns relative response rankings rather than the SFT token loss.
pretraining|responsible-use: Corpus provenance, unwanted associations and potential memorization shape responsible-use questions before downstream adaptation begins.
prompt-templates|quantized-models: A quantized local model still needs the correct tokenizer and prompt/chat template; compressed weights do not repair malformed input boundaries.
quantization|quantized-models: Quantization describes the representation change, while a quantized deployment format also depends on supported loading and execution kernels.
query-key-value|transformer-block: A block's attention sublayer projects representations into queries, keys and values before mixing information and applying its output projection.
representation-model|text-embedding: Representation models supply features; text embeddings are one reusable vector output whose pooling and scorer must match the task.
representation-model|word2vec: Word2vec learns static word vectors, a useful representation baseline distinct from contextual transformer features.
self-attention|transformer: Self-attention mixes information among positions within the sequence as part of a transformer block.
sentiment-analysis|task-specific-models: A sentiment classifier defines its label unit and domain; a task-specific checkpoint can learn that decision from labeled examples.
summarized-memory|windowed-memory: A window discards older turns by position; a summary compresses them and can introduce omissions or distortions.
supervised-classification|zero-shot-clas: Supervised classification fits task labels, whereas a zero-shot route applies an existing model without fitting those labels.
text-embedding|word2vec: Word2vec provides static word vectors; a sentence embedding requires an explicit composition or a model trained for text-level relationships.
token-embedding|tokenization: Tokenization supplies vocabulary IDs, which select the initial vectors in the token embedding table.
token|tokenization: A token is an output unit of tokenization; a tokenizer defines how text maps to units and IDs.
token|vocabulary: The vocabulary associates supported token strings or pieces with IDs; a token occurrence selects one of those entries.
vocabulary|word-and-subword-tokens: Word and subword tokenization choose different reusable units, affecting vocabulary size, rare words and sequence length.
